correctness.rationale: For two equally weighted observations, MAD squared equals variance identically, proving universal order agreement. A three-scenario equal-mean witness reverses the two rankings, the centered triple decomposition is exact, and padding by the common mean proves persistence for every larger support.

evidence: Konno and Yamazaki define portfolio standard deviation as the Markowitz L2 risk and mean absolute deviation as the L1 risk.
Their Theorem 3.1 proves exact proportionality MAD = sqrt(2/pi) times standard deviation under multivariate normal returns.
Their discussion motivates MAD partly because empirical stock returns need not be normal or symmetric and compares L1 and L2 portfolio models.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Normal-distribution proportionality is stronger than mere agreement inside that distributional class, but it does not imply the smallest finite empirical support at which non-proportionality can reverse a ranking.

value.rationale: Variance and mean absolute deviation are canonical competing portfolio risk measures. A sharp support threshold tells exactly when a finite scenario model becomes rich enough for the modeling choice to change a risk ranking. The equal-mean witness isolates dispersion alone, while the exact three-point decomposition identifies the structural source of the disagreement.
